analysis.title: Banks after the comeback: What comes next?
key_insights: European bank earnings expectations for FY2026 have been revised up +28% since 1 Feb 2024, the largest among Stoxx sectors, ahead of Energy +25% and Utilities +12%.
The bank recovery story is shifting from sector re-rating to an earnings and capital returns story, so selectivity matters more than owning the sector as a whole.
European bank earnings only regained 2007 levels in 2023, and analysts expect further increases in coming years.
European bank ROE has recovered to about 14%, near pre-financial-crisis levels, versus 4-7% in the low-rate era when banks traded below book and failed to cover cost of capital.
The rally does not mean the opportunity is exhausted, since higher profitability supports higher valuations and future returns come more from earnings growth and capital returns.
Balance sheet reinvestment is a multi-year tailwind: low-yielding long-term investments are maturing and being reinvested at higher yields, especially for banks in Italy, Spain, Greece and Portugal.
Southern European banks benefit from deposit margins lasting longer, as lending rates repriced quickly while deposit rates rose slowly.
Capital allocation matters more: large capital bases can fund dividends, buybacks, organic growth, technology and M&A. JPMorgan posted Q3 2026 net income of USD 15.3 billion as an example.
Regional earnings drivers diverge across Europe, the US and Asia, including rate cycles, loan growth, deposit competition, wealth management, payments and capital markets.
Regional risks differ: US commercial real estate and refinancing, European loan growth and deposit competition, and Asian credit quality and property markets.
The opportunity extends to insurers (better reinvestment yields) and asset and wealth managers (AUM growth and capital markets activity), favoring a global financials approach.

sector_views.rationale: Earnings revisions lead other sectors, ROE is near 14%, and reinvestment of maturing assets supports earnings for several years.
Insurers benefit from more attractive reinvestment yields.
They participate directly in rising AUM and capital markets development.

earnings_insights: JPMorgan Chase reported Q3 2026 net income of USD 15.3 billion (reported 13 October 2026), supported by growth in investment banking, payments, securities services and wealth management.
European bank FY2026 earnings forecasts (I/B/E/S consensus) are up 28% since 1 Feb 2024, as at 30 October 2026.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Back to pre-financial-crisis levels and above cost of capital, supporting higher price-to-book valuations.

risk_factors: US commercial real estate and refinancing risk.
Loan growth and deposit competition in Europe.
Credit quality and property markets in parts of Asia.
Part of the re-rating is already priced in, and banks are not risk-free.
Broad tailwind from rising interest rates is fading.

tension_points.bull_case: ROE near 14% and earnings upgrades mean the opportunity continues through earnings growth, capital returns and reinvestment tailwinds.
tension_points.bear_case: Valuations have moved well away from lows, the interest rate tailwind is fading, and regional credit and competition risks remain.

theme_stances.key_argument: The recovery is turning into an earnings story, with ROE back near 14% and reinvestment yields supporting earnings for several years.
theme_stances.evidence: the recovery story is increasingly turning into an earnings story
